title: Edge-count bound forcing a Hamiltonian cycle
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on $n$ vertices with $n \ge 3$. If the number of edges of $G$ exceeds $\binom{n-1}{2} + 1$, then $G$ is Hamiltonian, that is, $G$ contains a spanning cycle.
replaced:
Cor 4.6a: \texttt{$\varepsilon$ > C($\nu$$-$1,2) + 1} implies hamiltonicity.

If $G$ is a simple graph with $\nu \geq 3$ and
$\varepsilon > \binom{\nu-1}{2} + 1$, then $G$ is hamiltonian.
